pen.usage: Ticks, measured figures, numerals, active and focus states, link underlines, caret and selection; as a fill, the one primary button, measured bar spans, the current job and the closing sheet.

pen-hi.usage: Hover fill of the lime button; label of the ink button on hover.

pen-ink.usage: Writes on lime: label of the lime button, all text, rules and outlines on the closing sheet, fill of its primary button, selected text.

pen-ink-2.usage: Hover fill of the ink button only.

sheet.usage: Page, header, side rail, fill of plan blocks.

sheet-2.usage: The single tonal step: view frame, register row under the pointer or open, hover of outlined controls.

line.usage: Dividers inside tables and lists, header rule, zone-tick rules, tag outlines, year rulings. 1.3:1 on the sheet: structure only.

line-strong.usage: Sheet frame, sheet and block outlines, dimension lines, control outlines, group rules, to-scale bar track. 2.3:1 on the sheet: structure only.

ink.usage: Name, titles, table values, button labels. 17.6:1 on the sheet.

ink-3.usage: Labels, years and dates, zone ticks, sources, resting nav links, past jobs, arrows inside drawings. 6.9:1 on the sheet.

grid-minor.usage: 1px rulings every 1.5rem on the hero sheet and the plan.

grid-major.usage: 1px rulings every 6rem on the hero sheet and every 1.5rem inside the portrait's view frame.

display.purpose: The name in the hero, on two lines, uppercase; the closing question uses the same voice.

headline.purpose: Section titles, condensed and uppercase, joined to their measure by a dimension line.

title-lg.purpose: The main project's title, sentence case.

title.purpose: Process step and job titles; register titles flex around it.

block-title.purpose: Names of plan blocks, condensed caps; register group heads one step larger.

figure.purpose: Measured figures in the figures rail; smaller and lime when dimensioned on a plan block.

body.purpose: Default reading text; 1rem below 48rem; tabular lining figures.

body-sm.purpose: Notes, plan block text, table values.

label-strong.purpose: Buttons and the name beside the monogram, condensed caps.

label.purpose: Table terms, plan captions, client lines, section measures; uppercase, Label Gray.

data.purpose: Years and date ranges; tags and chain steps one step smaller. Sentence case.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: CSS var --ease. Exponential ease-out for everything that draws on load, rises, unfolds or nudges.

motion.name: frame-draw
motion.value: draw-x / draw-y (scale from 0) 1.1s var(--ease) both; delays 0s, 0.12s, 0.24s, 0.36s
motion.purpose: The four strokes of the hero frame plot clockwise on load.

motion.name: name-rise
motion.value: translateY(105%) to 0, 0.95s var(--ease) both; delay 0.15s, second line 0.24s
motion.purpose: Each line of the name rises out of its clipped line box.

motion.name: appear
motion.value: opacity 0 and translateY(0.75rem) to rest, 0.9s var(--ease) both; delays 0.45s, 0.53s, 0.62s
motion.purpose: Hero sentence, actions, links and rail on load; also the portrait toggle (0.8s at 0.9s) and the mobile menu (0.4s).

motion.name: view-frame-draw
motion.purpose: The portrait's view frame draws up from its base.

motion.name: portrait-develop
motion.value: opacity 0, translateY(1.5rem) and blur(6px) to rest, 1.2s var(--ease) both 0.35s
motion.purpose: The portrait develops once on load. The only blur in the system.

motion.name: scroll-draw
motion.value: draw-x linear both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 0% cover 28%
motion.purpose: Dimension lines, the step chain, the contract bracket, to-scale bars and job bars draw from their origin as they enter the viewport (draw-y for the step chain below 48rem). Behind @supports.

motion.name: scroll-progress
motion.value: scaleX(0) to scaleX(1) linear both; animation-timeline: scroll(root)
motion.purpose: The lime hairline under the sticky header grows with the page. Behind @supports.

motion.name: nav-underline
motion.value: transform scaleX(0) to scaleX(1), 0.4s var(--ease), origin left
motion.purpose: 1px lime underline on a nav link on hover and for the section in view.

motion.name: row-unfold
motion.value: grid-template-rows 0fr to 1fr, 0.55s var(--ease); detail opacity 0.5s after 0.12s (0.3s out)
motion.purpose: A register row unfolds in place.

motion.name: toggle-rotate
motion.purpose: The plus of a register toggle becomes a close mark.

motion.name: portrait-reveal
motion.value: --lr (registered <length>) 0 to 75rem in 0.9s var(--ease) for the avatar view, back to 0 in 0.6s; centered at 50% 30%, on the face
motion.purpose: The view toggle opens the illustrated portrait from the face and closes it again; hovering does nothing.

motion.name: state
motion.value: background-color, border-color and color 0.2s (0.25s on rows)

motion.name: icon-nudge
motion.value: translateY(3px) or translate(2px, -2px), 0.35s var(--ease); translate(3px, -3px) on closing-sheet rows
motion.purpose: The trailing icon moves in the direction of its action on hover.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { animation: none; transition-duration: 0.01ms } on every element and pseudo-element; scroll-behavior: auto
motion.purpose: Load and scroll drawing are removed and states switch at once, the portrait view included.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Below it the name beside the monogram is hidden (Tailwind max-sm).

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Below it: one column, 1rem body, drawings turn vertical.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Below it the text nav becomes a menu button (Tailwind lg).

breakpoints.name: sheet
breakpoints.purpose: Below it each rail folds under its main area.

breakpoints.name: short-desktop
breakpoints.purpose: The hero rail tightens and the revision row is hidden.

components.name: Plan Diagram

components.html:
Recorrido de un pedido

Gestión de pedidos

Cada sede enciende su cocina, pantalla de cocina, despacho y domiciliarios.

Punto de venta

Caja y cuadre, compras con impuestos, inventario por ubicación, producción en planta y 30 reportes.

Cobro: de 1,4 s a 0,7 s

Las tres hablan el mismo contrato de pedido, con transacciones e identificadores idempotentes: un pedido nunca se cobra dos veces.

narrative.overview:
The site is one technical drawing sheet of a developer's career. A charcoal sheet carries a faint drafting grid, warm light-gray linework and lettering from the DIN lineage. Lime is the only color and it behaves like a reviewer's pen: it ticks the ends of dimension lines, writes the measured figures, underlines what is active and fills one block per view. A claim is set the way a drawing sets it, as a figure beside its basis, and the systems he built are drawn as plans with blocks, arrows and brackets.

The density is that of a drawing, not of a landing page. The opening view is a framed sheet with zone ticks, the name in caps, a real cut-out portrait standing in a drawn view frame, and a side rail with numbered notes and a title block (role, location, work mode, engagement, languages, revision, CV). Each section opens with a condensed title joined by a dimension line to its measure. The main project is a bordered sheet holding a plan and a rail of figures, the other projects are register rows that unfold in place, the process is a dimension chain, experience is a timeline drawn to scale and the stack is a ruled table. The page ends on the only inverted sheet: lime ground, dark ink.

Motion has one idea: lines are drawn and content stays put. On load the frame plots its four strokes, the name rises out of its line box and the portrait develops. On scroll each dimension line, bracket and to-scale bar draws from its origin as it enters the viewport, and a lime hairline under the sticky header grows with the page. A two-button toggle swaps the photo for the illustrated avatar with a circular reveal from the face. All CSS motion is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. The direction contract refused the split hero with an avatar, the project card grid and the row of metric tiles; the owner's brief fixed the dark charcoal ground and the lime accent.
keyCharacteristics: One dark sheet (`color-scheme: dark`); there is no light theme.
One accent, lime, used as a pen: ticks, measured figures, active and focus states, one filled block per view.
One superfamily in two widths: Sofia Sans for the name, titles and sentences; Sofia Sans Condensed for section titles, labels, figures and controls. No monospace.
Square corners everywhere; the portrait reveal is the only circle.
1px linework carries all structure: frame, title blocks, dimension lines, plan blocks. No shadows.
Measurements are real: bars and the timeline are drawn to scale from the content data.
Lines draw, content stays put, and all CSS motion is removed under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Reviewer's Pen Rule
rules.body: Lime marks what a reviewer would mark: the ticks that close a dimension line, a measured figure, the numeral of a note or step, the active nav item, the pressed toggle, focus, the underline of a link. It never colors a heading or running text, and it never outlines a container at rest.

rules.name: The One Lime Block Rule
rules.body: A view holds at most one lime-filled block: the primary action in the hero, then the closing sheet. Every other lime fill is a measurement or a mark: the measured span of a to-scale bar, the current job on the timeline, the 6px corner of the monogram, selected text.

rules.name: The Structure-Only Line Rule
rules.body: Object Line and Hairline sit at 2.3:1 and 1.3:1 on the sheet, so a line organizes but never carries meaning alone. Every outlined control also holds a text label or an icon at text contrast, and every bar has its figure written beside it.

rules.name: The Width Is Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Normal width is for language: the name, project and role titles, sentences. Condensed is for lettering: section titles, labels, figures, dates, controls. A new element picks its width by that test; a second family or a monospace is never the answer.

rules.name: The Lettering Caps Rule
rules.body: Uppercase belongs to the name, the closing question, section titles and condensed labels and controls, tracked 0.06em to 0.09em at label sizes. Project titles, figures, tags and sentences stay in sentence case.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums` is set once on the body, so every figure, year and date aligns in columns wherever it appears.

rules.name: The Inhabited Rail Rule
rules.body: The right-hand rail is where a drawing keeps its notes: numbered notes and the title block in the hero, measured figures beside the plan. A rail is never empty and never decorative, and below 72rem it folds under what it annotates.

rules.name: The One Grid Per Entry Rule
rules.body: A register row and its unfolded detail sit on the same four columns, and experience and stack share the 10rem label column, so the same field is found in the same place down the page.

rules.name: The Space Above Rule
rules.body: A section is announced by the space above its title, not by a rule or a tinted band. The only full-width change of ground is the closing sheet.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats and nothing casts. A surface may step one tone under the pointer or while open; rank is shown by inversion to lime, once, at the end of the page.

rules.name: The Line-and-Tick Rule
rules.body: One geometry draws everything: a 1px line closed by a 1px lime tick. Frame, dividers, dimension lines, active states and scroll progress are all that same line; nothing gets a thicker border to look important.

rules.name: The Grid Under Drawings Rule
rules.body: The drafting grid appears only under things that are drawings: the hero sheet (masked so it is strongest around the portrait), the portrait's view frame and the main project's plan. Tables, the register, the timeline and the closing sheet sit on plain sheet.

dos: Do draw structure with 1px lines: `line` for dividers inside a table or list, `line-strong` for outlines, frames and dimension lines.
Do close a dimension line with 1px × 11px lime ticks and end it on a real measure set in Label.
Do keep lime for marks, measured figures, active and focus states, and one filled block per view.
Do choose width by role: Sofia Sans for names, titles and sentences; Sofia Sans Condensed for section titles, labels, figures, dates and controls.
Do write a figure with its basis: the value in Figure, one sentence of scope or source under it, and a to-scale bar only when the value is a ratio of two real numbers.
Do keep every project on the register grid with the same spec fields; when code is private the field stays and says so with the lock icon.
Do number only what is ordered: hero notes and process steps carry a lime condensed numeral, sections carry none.
Do put a label beside or under what it names: the measure at the end of the dimension line, the client line under the project title.

Do build new motion as a line growing from its origin (`scaleX` or `scaleY`, `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` on load, a scroll-linked `view()` timeline below the hero), and make sure the `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block stops it.
Do use Lucide outline icons at about 1rem, with a text label beside them or an accessible name on a square toggle, and 1px square-capped SVG for arrows inside drawings.
donts: Don't round corners or cast shadows; the portrait reveal is the only circle and nothing floats.
Don't put content on cards, lay projects out as a card grid or set figures as a row of metric tiles; projects are register rows and figures live in a ruled rail beside the plan they measure.
Don't add a second accent, a gradient fill, gradient text or glass; the only gradients are the 1px grid rulings and the masks that fade them.
Don't set headings or running text in lime, and don't fill a second block with lime in the same view.
Don't bring in a second typeface or a monospace, and don't let a system face stand in for Sofia Sans in display sizes.
Don't place a small label above a heading; the heading speaks first.
Don't draw the drafting grid under tables, the register, the timeline or the closing sheet.
Don't animate content on scroll; below the hero only lines, brackets and bars draw.
Don't rely on a line alone to show a control or a state; Object Line is 2.3:1 on the sheet.
Don't add a light theme; the sheet is dark only.
